questions.q: Do you work or are you a student?
questions.model: I'm a student at the moment, studying business management at university. It's been a steep learning curve, but I find it rewarding because we get to grips with real business problems and gain hands-on experience. Last term, for example, we ran a mock company, which taught me a lot about teamwork.

vocab.meaning: a situation where you have to learn a lot very quickly
vocab.example: Starting my first job in a hospital was a steep learning curve.

vocab.meaning: to begin to understand and deal with something difficult
vocab.example: It took me a few weeks to get to grips with the new software.

vocab.meaning: practical knowledge gained by actually doing something
vocab.example: Employers prefer graduates who already have some hands-on experience in the field.

vocab.meaning: giving you a feeling of satisfaction or benefit
vocab.example: Teaching young children is tiring but incredibly rewarding work.

phrases: It's been a ..., but I find it ...

questions.q: Why did you choose that subject or job?
questions.model: Honestly, it was partly down to my parents, who run a small shop. Watching them weigh up risks every day sparked my interest in how companies survive. I also felt a business degree would open doors for me, and I wanted to be my own boss one day.

vocab.meaning: to think carefully about the good and bad points before deciding
vocab.example: You should weigh up the costs before buying a second car.

vocab.meaning: create new chances and opportunities for you
vocab.example: Speaking fluent English can open doors in the international job market.

vocab.meaning: to run your own business instead of working for someone else
vocab.example: Many freelancers love the freedom to be their own boss.

vocab.meaning: caused a feeling or interest to begin
vocab.example: A documentary about space sparked my interest in physics years ago.

phrases: Honestly, it was partly down to ...

questions.q: What do you find most difficult about your studies or work?
questions.model: Probably time management. Several tight deadlines often land in the same week, so I end up juggling assignments and part-time shifts, and sometimes I burn the midnight oil. A weekly schedule helps me stay on top of things.

vocab.meaning: dates for finishing work that leave very little time
vocab.example: Journalists regularly work under tight deadlines and enormous pressure.

vocab.meaning: to work or study very late into the night
vocab.example: Before the final exams, everyone in my class was burning the midnight oil.

vocab.meaning: to manage your tasks well without feeling overwhelmed
vocab.example: Keeping a diary helps me stay on top of things at work.

vocab.meaning: trying to manage several tasks at the same time
vocab.example: She is juggling a full-time job and evening classes this year.

phrases: ... helps me stay on top of things.

questions.q: Would you like to change your job or studies in the future?
questions.model: Not completely, but I'd love to specialise in marketing after my degree. I'm fascinated by how brands sway people's choices, and I think it would play to my strengths, since I'm quite creative. Of course, plans can change, so I'm keeping an open mind.

vocab.meaning: to focus on one particular area of study or work
vocab.example: After two years as a nurse, she decided to specialise in children's care.

vocab.meaning: to use the things you are naturally good at
vocab.example: A role in sales would play to his strengths as a talker.

vocab.meaning: being ready to consider new ideas or possibilities
vocab.example: I'm keeping an open mind about moving abroad for work.

vocab.meaning: to influence someone's opinion or decision
vocab.example: Celebrity adverts can sway young shoppers more than we realise.

phrases: I think it would play to my strengths.
Of course, plans can change, so ...

questions.q: Where is your hometown, and what is it like?
questions.model: I come from Da Nang, a coastal city in central Vietnam. It has a laid-back pace of life compared with Hanoi, and it's renowned for its long sandy beaches. What I love is that you get the best of both worlds: you can be at the sea or up in the mountains within half an hour.

vocab.meaning: a relaxed way of living where nobody is in a hurry
vocab.example: Many tourists fall in love with the laid-back pace of life on the islands.

vocab.meaning: famous and respected because of a particular quality
vocab.example: The region is renowned for its excellent seafood and warm hospitality.

vocab.meaning: the advantages of two different things at the same time
vocab.example: Living in the suburbs gives you the best of both worlds.

vocab.meaning: located on or near the sea
vocab.example: We spent the weekend in a quiet coastal village near Hue.

phrases: I come from ..., a ... city in ...

questions.q: Do you think your hometown is a good place for young people?
questions.model: Mostly, yes. It's safe and the cost of living is reasonable, so young people can afford to rent their own place. The only drawback is the lack of job prospects, which is why many graduates move to bigger cities, leading to a brain drain.

vocab.meaning: the amount of money needed to pay for everyday life
vocab.example: The cost of living in big cities keeps rising every year.

vocab.meaning: the chances of finding good work in the future
vocab.example: Graduates with strong language skills usually have excellent job prospects.

vocab.meaning: the loss of educated people who leave a place to work elsewhere
vocab.example: Poor salaries have caused a brain drain from many rural areas.

vocab.meaning: a disadvantage or negative point
vocab.example: The main drawback of living downtown is the constant noise.

phrases: The only drawback is the lack of ...

questions.q: What changes have happened in your hometown in recent years?
questions.model: Quite a lot, actually. A new bridge and several shopping malls have sprung up, so the city feels far more modern. Traffic is a bit frustrating at rush hour, but on the whole I think the development has improved people's quality of life.

vocab.meaning: appeared or developed quickly and unexpectedly
vocab.example: New cafes have sprung up all along the riverside this year.

vocab.meaning: the busy time when many people travel to or from work
vocab.example: I avoid driving during rush hour whenever I possibly can.

vocab.meaning: taking everything into account; in general
vocab.example: On the whole, the new metro line has been a great success.

vocab.meaning: how comfortable and satisfying daily life is
vocab.example: Clean air and green parks improve the quality of life here.

phrases: Traffic is a bit frustrating at ...
..., but on the whole I think ...

questions.q: What is the weather usually like in your country?
questions.model: It varies a lot depending on the region. In the south it's hot and humid all year round, whereas the north has a proper winter with bitterly cold, damp days. Personally, I find the summer heat unbearable, so I tend to stay indoors in the afternoons.

vocab.meaning: during every season of the year without a break
vocab.example: You can swim in the sea all year round in my region.

vocab.meaning: extremely and painfully cold
vocab.example: It was bitterly cold on the mountain, even with two jackets on.

vocab.meaning: to remain inside a building instead of going out
vocab.example: During the storm, the authorities told everyone to stay indoors.

vocab.meaning: so bad that you can hardly accept or tolerate it
vocab.example: The noise from the building site next door was unbearable.

phrases: It varies a lot depending on ...

questions.q: Which season do you like best, and why?
questions.model: I'd say autumn, without a doubt. The weather is mild, the skies are clear and there's a gentle breeze, so it's ideal for being out and about. I often take my camera to the lake near my house, because the evening light is simply stunning.

vocab.meaning: certainly; there is no question about it
vocab.example: Without a doubt, this is the best coffee in town.

vocab.meaning: a soft, light wind
vocab.example: A gentle breeze made the afternoon by the river very pleasant.

vocab.meaning: active and moving around outside the home
vocab.example: My grandfather is eighty but still out and about every morning.

vocab.meaning: extremely beautiful and impressive
vocab.example: The view from the top of the hill was absolutely stunning.

questions.q: Does the weather affect your mood?
questions.model: Definitely. When it's grey and drizzling for days, I feel sluggish, a bit under the weather, and find it hard to concentrate. On the other hand, a bright sunny morning lifts my spirits, and I get a lot more done, so the weather clearly takes a toll on my mood.

vocab.meaning: feeling slightly ill or low in energy
vocab.example: I'm feeling a little under the weather, so I'll stay in bed.

vocab.meaning: makes me feel happier and more positive
vocab.example: Listening to my favourite songs always lifts my spirits quickly.

vocab.meaning: causes gradual harm or tiredness to someone or something
vocab.example: Working night shifts for years takes a toll on your health.

vocab.meaning: slow, tired and lacking energy
vocab.example: I always feel sluggish after eating a very heavy lunch.

phrases: ..., so the weather clearly takes a toll on ...

cue.topic: Describe a teacher who influenced you
bullets: how the teacher taught or behaved in class
and explain why this teacher influenced you

part2.model: I'd like to talk about my English teacher from high school, Mrs Lan, who had a huge influence on me. She taught us for three years, and she was in her forties when I first met her. At first, I was painfully shy and terrified of speaking in front of others. What made her special was her patience. She never laughed at our mistakes, and instead she created a nurturing atmosphere where we saw them as a natural part of learning. In class, she was full of energy and always walked around the room to check on us. She used songs, short films and role-plays, so the lessons were never dull. I remember one occasion when I forgot my words during a presentation. She simply smiled, gave me a hint and waited, and that small gesture boosted my confidence enough to carry on. Looking back, I think she influenced me in two ways. First, she ignited my passion for languages, which is why I'm studying English today. Second, she pushed me to step out of my comfort zone, and that taught me that confidence matters as much as talent. She could always bring out the best in every student, so nobody felt left behind. Even now, whenever I feel nervous, I hear her voice telling me to take a breath and try again. Honestly, I'm really grateful to her for everything.

vocab.meaning: to help someone show their best qualities and abilities
vocab.example: A good coach knows how to bring out the best in a young team.

vocab.word: step out of my comfort zone
vocab.meaning: to try something new that feels difficult or uncomfortable
vocab.example: Joining the debating club made me step out of my comfort zone.

vocab.meaning: started a strong and lasting interest in something
vocab.example: A school trip to the museum ignited my passion for history.

vocab.meaning: made me feel more sure of my own abilities
vocab.example: Winning the poetry prize really boosted my confidence at school.

vocab.meaning: thinking about the past from the present
vocab.example: Looking back, moving abroad was the best choice I ever made.

vocab.meaning: caring and supportive in a way that helps people grow
vocab.example: The kindergarten has a warm and nurturing environment for every child.

structure: Opening: name the teacher and say you will explain the influence
Who and what: subject, how long you studied with them, how you met
Teaching style: two or three concrete details of how they behaved in class
A specific story or memory that shows their character
Why they influenced you: two clear effects on your life
Closing: a short reflection on how you feel about them now

roundingOff.q: Do you still keep in touch with this teacher?
roundingOff.model: Yes, I do, although not as often as I'd like. We keep in touch on social media a few times a year, and I always send her a heartfelt card on Teachers' Day. Next time I'm back home, I'm hoping to pay her a visit and thank her in person.

vocab.meaning: to stay in contact with someone
vocab.example: We still keep in touch even though I live abroad.

vocab.meaning: to go and see someone at their home or workplace
vocab.example: I plan to pay her a visit before I fly back.

vocab.meaning: face to face rather than by phone or message
vocab.example: I would prefer to say sorry in person rather than by text.

vocab.meaning: sincere and coming from deep feeling
vocab.example: She sent me a heartfelt letter after my grandfather passed away.

Next time I'm back, I'm hoping to ...

questions.q: What qualities make a good teacher?
questions.model: I think patience and passion matter most. A teacher who genuinely loves the subject can make even dry topics come alive, and a patient one gives students room to make mistakes. On top of that, good teachers cater to different learning styles, because not everybody picks up information in the same way. For instance, some pupils need visual examples, while others learn better through discussion. In the end, it is the human connection that students remember long after the exam.

vocab.meaning: to become interesting, vivid and full of energy
vocab.example: History really comes alive when you visit the places in person.

vocab.meaning: to provide what a particular group of people needs
vocab.example: The school tries to cater to students with very different abilities.

vocab.meaning: the different ways in which people prefer to study and remember
vocab.example: Some learning styles work better for visual thinkers than for listeners.

vocab.meaning: in addition to what has just been said
vocab.example: On top of that, the course is completely free for all residents.

phrases: In the end, it is ... that ...

questions.q: Is it better to study in a big class or a small class?
questions.model: Generally speaking, smaller classes are more effective because the teacher can give each student individual attention, and pupils feel less intimidated about asking questions. That said, large classes have their advantages, as they expose students to a wide range of perspectives. In my view, the ideal size depends on the subject, since practical lessons clearly need fewer students than lectures. Personally, I learned best in a group of about fifteen, where discussion felt natural and relaxed, and nobody could hide at the back.

vocab.meaning: time and care given to one person separately
vocab.example: Private tutors can give children plenty of individual attention.

vocab.meaning: many different ways of looking at the same issue
vocab.example: A diverse team brings a wide range of perspectives to every project.

vocab.meaning: used to add a point that limits what was just said
vocab.example: That said, online lessons can still be lonely for some learners.

vocab.meaning: feeling frightened or nervous because of someone or something
vocab.example: New employees often feel intimidated in their first meetings.

phrases: In my view, the ideal ... depends on ...

questions.q: Should schools focus more on exams or on practical skills?
questions.model: Ideally, schools should strike a balance, but at present many lean heavily on exams. Students end up learning by rote without really understanding the material, and they leave school unprepared for real work. I believe teaching skills like problem-solving and communication would serve them better, although exams still matter as a fair way to measure progress. A mix of both would equip young people with the tools they need for university and the workplace.

vocab.meaning: to find a fair middle point between two competing things
vocab.example: It is hard to strike a balance between work and family.

vocab.meaning: to depend very much on one thing
vocab.example: Some universities lean heavily on final exams for grading.

vocab.meaning: memorising facts by repetition without understanding them
vocab.example: Learning by rote may help you pass tests but rarely lasts.

vocab.meaning: the ability to find answers to difficult situations
vocab.example: Employers look for strong problem-solving skills in graduates.

phrases: Ideally, ... should strike a balance, but ...
I believe ... would serve them better.

questions.q: What are the advantages and disadvantages of learning online?
questions.model: The main advantage is flexibility. Students can fit lessons around their jobs, and people in remote villages can take courses from top universities at a fraction of the cost. On the downside, it takes a great deal of self-discipline, because a phone can easily pull you away from your studies. There is also less face-to-face interaction, so learners can feel isolated. On balance, I think online study works best as a supplement to classroom teaching rather than a replacement.

vocab.word: at a fraction of the cost
vocab.meaning: for a much lower price than the usual one
vocab.example: You can learn Spanish from native speakers at a fraction of the cost.

vocab.meaning: used to introduce a disadvantage or negative point
vocab.example: On the downside, living near the airport means constant noise.

vocab.meaning: the ability to make yourself do things without being forced
vocab.example: Training for a marathon demands real self-discipline and patience.

vocab.meaning: direct communication between people who are in the same place
vocab.example: Children still need plenty of face-to-face interaction to develop social skills.

phrases: On balance, I think ... works best as ...

questions.q: Do you think university education should be free for everyone?
questions.model: In an ideal world, yes, because education benefits the whole society, not just the individual. Free tuition would create a level playing field for talented students from poor families. Having said that, governments have limited budgets, so a more realistic option might be generous scholarships and low-interest loans, which would widen access without placing a huge burden on taxpayers. It would also encourage more families to see university as a realistic goal for their children.

vocab.meaning: a situation in which everyone has a fair and equal chance
vocab.example: Anonymous exams help create a level playing field for all candidates.

vocab.meaning: to make something available to more people
vocab.example: The new law aims to widen access to higher education.

vocab.meaning: used to introduce a contrasting point after agreeing
vocab.example: Having said that, I understand why some people disagree with the plan.

vocab.meaning: money given to a student to pay for their studies
vocab.example: Several scholarships are available for students with excellent grades.

phrases: a more realistic option might be ...
